acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

params.blockNumber: EVM `block.number` of the current block (idempotency key). NOT        trusted as an epoch tag — the epoch is derived from it, because the block number        is deterministic over agreed state while a proposer-supplied tag is not.
params.leaderIndex: The producer's position in the epoch committee, already checked at        vote time against the consensus-supplied round leader.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

blocksInEpoch(uint64).notice: Blocks recorded for `epoch`. Equal to the epoch length for a complete epoch —         a shortfall is what the derived partial-epoch taint keys on. Also the free         mid-epoch health probe: inside epoch E the healthy invariant is         `blocksInEpoch(E) == block.number - first(E) + 1`, which surfaces an unrecorded         block within one polling interval instead of at the close a day later.

getProductionStats(address,uint64).notice: The delegator-facing signal. `kickCount` and `lastFailedEpoch` are the         actionable pair; permanent removal stays the delegators' call.

lastProcessedBlock().notice: The most recent block for which `recordProduction` fired. Ops signal that the         executor pipeline is alive, and the epoch cursor's own backing store.

pendingExclusions().notice: Validators currently serving an exclusion. Length is the concurrent count the         `<= f` ceiling is enforced against.

producedAt(uint64,uint32).notice: Blocks credited to committee index `idx` in `epoch`.

readmitAtEpoch(address).notice: The epoch at whose close `validator` is released, or 0 when not excluded.         Read by governance activation so re-activating a validator cannot silently         cancel a pending exclusion.

recordProduction(uint64,uint8).notice: Record one block's producer. Injected once per block by the executor.

documentation.text:
@notice Emitted when an epoch closes with fewer recorded blocks than the epoch length.
         MANDATORY, not diagnostic: the partial-epoch taint is DERIVED from the block
         count rather than stored, so a single unrecorded block silently costs the whole
         epoch its verdicts — a full day at production pacing. Without this event the
         tier can sit inert for months while reading as enabled. Alert on any
         occurrence; on two consecutive ones read the tier as OFF regardless of the kill
         flag. Epoch 0 is partial BY CONSTRUCTION (the ahead-commit driver runs after
         the recorder in the same block, so genesis blocks park) — exempt it.

@notice Emitted when more than `f` members fail for the FIRST time in one epoch: an
         environment, not individual faults. No stamps that close.

@dev Gas forwarded to the stipend leg. Bounds the contiguous settle catch-up so an
      out-of-gas inside it cannot take the close down with it. Sized against the
      measured ~2.4M per settled epoch and `MAX_SETTLE_CATCHUP`, inside the 30M
      hardcoded system-call ceiling that the whole close must fit.

@dev Close epoch `epoch`. Three legs, in this order and for this reason: releases first
      so an expiring exclusion cannot be held hostage by the guard; verdicts second and
      FAIL-LOUD, because a rolled-back no-op would retry every block forever and the
      only symptom would be a warning; the stipend last and TOLERANT, behind its own gas
      bound, because it is the one leg where a frozen payment is preferable to any
      chance of a frozen chain.
@dev Release every exclusion whose term has expired. Bounded by `f`.

@dev The verdict sweep for a fully recorded epoch.
      `due_i = w_i / W * recorded` is an EXPECTATION from on-chain stake, not a replay of
      the leader lottery — mirroring the election on-chain is forbidden by construction.
      `w_i` is the FROZEN weight stamped at commit from the selection epoch, i.e. the
      exact weight the lottery drew with, which is what makes the expectation exact
      rather than approximate. Both predicates are cross-multiplied: no division, no
      fixed point.
      What this measures, and why it cannot be tripped by a bad network: with a fresh
      leader draw at every view, the share credited to member `i` is
      `(w_i/W) * q_i / q̄`, so failing below half of `due` means the member's per-slot
      success rate is below HALF THE STAKE-WEIGHTED FLEET AVERAGE. Uniform degradation
      moves every member together and fails nobody, at any severity. A dead member has
      `produced == 0` with certainty and fails at every dilution level.

@dev At most two stamps per close, never more than `f` concurrent. The order is
      kick-count descending then address ascending — stated rather than left to storage
      iteration order, which is deterministic but is an accident a future layout change
      could silently alter with no spec to violate.

@dev Per-close stamp cap. Deliberately low: a correlated loss of `f` seats is answered
      over at least eight closes, which gives a healed cause time to clear the verdicts
      before most stamps land — verdicts do not accumulate, so a recovered member simply
      passes its next epoch.

documentation.text:
@title ProductionLiveness
 @author Fluent Labs
 @notice Records WHO PRODUCED each block and, at the epoch close, temporarily excludes any
         committee member that produced fewer than half the blocks its stake made it due.
 @dev Replaces `LivenessSlashing`, whose signal was a proposer-asserted vote bitmap that no
      verifier could check — one Byzantine proposer wrote whatever it liked, which is why the
      jail it fed shipped kill-switched. The 2-byte `[version][leader_index]` record this
      contract consumes is checked by every honest voter against the consensus-supplied round
      leader, so forging it needs the full `n − f` quorum instead of one proposer.
      What the consequence is FOR, since "downtime" alone would not justify it: a seat that
      does not produce wastes its share of the block schedule whatever the cause (at n=51,
      ~2% of views per epoch, forever), and an abandoned seat additionally consumes the
      zero-slack fault budget with nothing else to reclaim it — for a self-staked dead
      validator the delegator loop cannot fire, because the delegator IS the dead operator.
      Exclusion is never a slash: it is temporary, auto-reversing, rate-limited and refused
      when no replacement exists.
